notes.content: The page defines Multomb(F) as the grande or M-multiombre of F, an ensembliste figure in M indexed faithfully by the unfolding F-tilde, whose knowledge implies knowledge of F. It then introduces the inclusion L into M and the two corresponding inverse-image applications. Composition with the cited 1.6 a)b) produces (1.9): a map from the script F to P(L), F sent to omb(F), and a map from the script F to Fig(L), F sent to multomb(F). The author says the first has no reason to be injective and qualifies the second as having a tendency to be so. The final lines name the petite ombre and petite multiombre. The page contains definitions and a qualification, not a supplied proof.
math_reading_decisions: The double-stem F after M-multiombre is retained as mathbb F from the ink; it is not silently normalized to the ordinary F used elsewhere and is not interpreted as a new object.

The P alphabet remains uncertain between mathcal and mathscr at its first occurrence. Subsequent occurrences use mathcal as the stipulated first candidate. Script F is represented by mathcal F, distinct from the plain F in the element mappings.

The inverse-image Fig arrow has only an upper barb. It is transcribed literally as rightharpoonup even though the surrounding prose calls it an application. No special partial-map or categorical meaning is supplied from that shape alone.

The visible cancelled left hooks in both rows of (1.9) are preserved. The surviving right-facing arrows are read as the live map directions. The injectivity sentence is not used as a substitute for observing the cancelled strokes.
The t of the displayed multomb is heavily overwritten. The transcription marks live/retraced t versus cancelled t as alternatives without inventing an earlier letter or an insertion chronology.
The cited 1.6 a)b) was not inspected because it is outside the assigned page. Local domain/codomain and function-name parsing was performed, not a reconstruction of the preceding argument.
The indexing insertion says fidèlement and déployement. The latter spelling is preserved despite the modern déploiement form in H.
The small cross after l'être has no visible corresponding note on this page. It is preserved without fabricating a note or treating it as a mathematical multiplication operation.
author_doubts: “dont la première n'a aucune raison d'être injective” is an explicit limitation of what is being asserted.
“la seconde par contre a une tendance à l'être” is the cautious formulation, quoted with the first reading of the unresolved la seconde|le second locus. A small cross follows l'être.
No explicit vérifier, à voir, question mark, proof request, or independent authorial check instruction was found on this page.

check_events.outcome: Read the claim that knowing Multomb(F) implies knowing F and the faithful-indexing qualification. No local conflict was found in its wording; no proof or verification of the claim was undertaken.

Checked that the written maps go from M-based objects to L-based objects along the displayed inclusion L into M. No domain reversal or missing index was found. Literal arrowhead shape was checked separately from the expected map notation.

Compared both domain letters, codomains, plain input F and named outputs. The pairs parse as the two announced compositions; the overwritten t remains a visual uncertainty. The external reference 1.6 was not checked.
Identified a non-injectivity caveat for the first map and a tentative qualification for the second. These are carried as authorial statements, not promoted to a theorem or proved.

Read the lowercase omb and multomb names against their two displayed outputs and the grande/petite distinction. The barred m is retained as an abbreviation, with its probable expansion confined to notes.
